children: The AIB Ireland Construction PMI eased to 50.7 in August 2026 from 53.0 in July, signaling a second consecutive monthly increase in construction activity, albeit at marginal pace.
Growth was concentrated in the commercial sector, where activity rose for the sixth time in seven months, while civil engineering was broadly unchanged and housing activity declined solidly.
New orders expanded for a second consecutive month, with the pace of growth accelerating to a five-month high, while stronger project pipelines lifted business confidence to a six-month high.
Firms also increased input buying for the first time in three months, although employment growth slowed to a 10-month low.

Input cost inflation accelerated, with oil and metals cited as key sources of higher costs, while supplier delivery times lengthened at the fastest pace in four months amid stock shortages and courier constraints.
The use of subcontractors increased for a ninth consecutive month, though the pace of growth eased.

title: Ireland Construction Expands for Second Month
